framework: China - Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services (Order No. 15, in force 15 Aug 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Applies to services using generative AI to provide text, images, audio or video to the public in mainland China; R&D not offered to the domestic public is outside scope.

framework: China - GB/T 45654-2025 Cybersecurity Technology: Basic Safety Requirements for Generative AI Services (effective 1 Nov 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: At least 90% of sampled outputs must be free of the listed risk types.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Training, validation and testing data must be governed by documented practices including examination for biases and measures to detect and mitigate them; data sets must be relevant, sufficiently representative, as error-free and complete as possible, and reflect the geographic, contextual, behavioural or functional setting of intended use.
what_is_tested: Data quality, representativeness and bias of train/validation/test sets

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Notified-body certificates are valid for the period stated, at most five years for Annex I systems and four years for Annex III systems, extendable at the provider's request after re-assessment; where a system no longer meets Section 2 requirements the body must, applying proportionality, suspend, withdraw or restrict the certificate unless the provider takes corrective action within the deadline set by the body.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Systemic-risk GPAI providers must assess and mitigate systemic risks at Union level, track and report serious incidents to the AI Office, and ensure adequate cybersecurity for the model and its physical infrastructure.
what_is_tested: Systemic risk assessment/mitigation; incident reporting; cybersecurity

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluations must be scientifically rigorous (internal validity, external validity, reproducibility) and use state-of-the-art elicitation that minimises under-elicitation and model deception (e.g. sandbagging), matching misuse actors' elicitation capability and expected deployment context.

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Adds requirements for bodies that audit and certify AI management systems under ISO/IEC 42001, supplementing ISO/IEC 17021-1; published 7 July 2025, 31 pages, stage 60.60.
what_is_tested: Competence and consistency of certification bodies

framework: Japan - Outline of AI Guidelines for Business Ver. 1.1 (MIC/METI, 4 Apr 2025; provisional translation)
requirement_paraphrase: AI business users are to understand the precision and risks of AI output and confirm risk factors before use.
what_is_tested: User-side confirmation of output precision and risk

framework: South Korea - AI Framework Act (AI Basic Act)
requirement_paraphrase: Fines of up to KRW 30 million for failing Art. 31(1) notice, failing to appoint domestic representative, or ignoring an Art. 40(3) order.

framework: NCA AI Cybersecurity Guidelines (draft, AICG-1:2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends periodic testing of backup, recovery and rollback procedures for AI systems.

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
clause_or_page: Outcome 2.1 / Process 2.1.1, p.14 (technical testing, traditional AI)
requirement_paraphrase: For each model, run explainability methods to help users understand drivers of the model's output.
who_tests: AI system owner using AI Verify toolkit

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: A risk assessment must be done for all AI systems and related assets; risks are tracked in a register with assigned owners.

framework: ADGM Office of Data Protection - Guidance on DPR 2021 Part 4 (DPIA)
requirement_paraphrase: A DPIA is required before processing likely to create high risk, and the guidance lists as triggers use of personal data in datasets used to train or refine an AI system (in the specific exception context) and profiling or automated decision-making used to decide access to a service or benefit.
what_is_tested: The planned processing, including AI training data use and ADM: risks to individuals

framework: Dubai AI System Ethics Self-Assessment Tool (Digital Dubai, beta)
requirement_paraphrase: Developer or operator organisations can self-assess the ethics level of an AI system (fairness, accountability, transparency, explainability) from idea stage to operation. The guidelines are recommended, not compulsory. The page suggests not proceeding with implementation unless a certain ethics performance level is reached, and says the tool is for self-assessment only and is not audited, checked or regulated.
what_is_tested: Self-judged ethics performance across four aspects, by decision significance (non-significant, significant, critical)

framework: DHA Artificial Intelligence in the Healthcare Policy (HISHD/PP-09)
requirement_paraphrase: End users must conduct regular audits of AI functionality by an independent third party, reporting to DHA-HRS as needed.
what_is_tested: Functionality of deployed healthcare AI (periodic audit)
who_tests: Independent third party engaged by end users; DHA-HRS receives reports

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Discrimination impact assessments could be considered before release; the guideline says the timing and documentation of results and mitigations should be addressed.

framework: Federal Decree-Law 45/2021 (PDPL)
requirement_paraphrase: Controllers and processors must adopt security measures including a process for testing and evaluating the effectiveness of those measures.
what_is_tested: Effectiveness of security measures for personal data processing

framework: UK DSIT Introduction to AI assurance (published 2024-02-12)
requirement_paraphrase: Lists a spectrum of assurance mechanisms - risk assessment, impact assessment, bias audit, compliance audit, conformity assessment (often including performance testing), formal verification - to be used in combination across the AI lifecycle, proportionate to risk.
who_tests: Internal teams or third-party assurance providers

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: The Framework is intended to be voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific and use-case agnostic.

framework: US NIST AI 800-2 ipd (CAISI) Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models (Initial Public Draft, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Design the evaluation protocol, write evaluation code, run and track results, and debug the evaluation; common bugs include degraded serving; evaluation cheating and evaluation awareness are listed as bugs tagged [Emerging Practice].
